content: The biological subfamily Bovinae encompasses a diverse group of ten genera of medium to large-sized ungulates. This group includes domestic cattle, bison, water buffalo, yaks, and antelopes with either four horns or spiral-shaped horns. The evolutionary relationships among the members of this subfamily remain unclear, and their classification into loosely defined tribes rather than formal sub-groups reflects this uncertainty. Members of the Bovinae subfamily generally share certain characteristics, such as cloven hooves and the presence of true horns in at least one sex of each species. In most countries, bovines are primarily utilized as a source of food. Cattle, in particular, are consumed almost universally, with the notable exception of India, where bovines are regarded as sacred animals by Hindus. The term Bos is derived from the Greek word Βοῦς (Vus), which translates to ox.
